supply_chain.source: NY Fed Global Supply Chain Pressure Index (GSCPI)
supply_chain.raw_value: GSCPI +1.28 (Sep 2026) | WEI +3.33 (context, not scored) | BDRY $12.57 (context, not scored)
supply_chain.raw_label: Global Supply Chain Pressure (z-score; 0 = historical average)
supply_chain.description: The NY Fed's Global Supply Chain Pressure Index combines transport costs and supplier delivery times across major economies into one z-score, where 0 is the historical average. It stood at +1.28 for September 2026: supply chain pressure is well above its historical average. The score's normal (80) is the pre-2020 median. The index already includes the Baltic Dry Index, so the BDRY dry-bulk ETF and the Weekly Economic Index are shown for context and are not scored.
supply_chain.calculation: GSCPI is mapped through fixed anchors, lower being better: the healthiest 5% of pre-2020 months = 100, the pre-2020 median = 80, the worst month on record = 0. The NY Fed publishes about 5 days after the month ends. BDRY and WEI are not part of the score.

inputs.name: gscpi
inputs.source: NY Fed Global Supply Chain Pressure Index (GSCPI)

chokepoints.raw_label: Three weakest corridors, 7-day average transits as % of normal
chokepoints.description: Share of normal ship traffic still passing through eight chokepoints: Malacca, Taiwan Strait, Gibraltar, Hormuz, Dover, Red Sea (the worse of Bab el-Mandeb and Suez), Bosporus and Panama. A closed corridor means delayed or rerouted cargo. Cape of Good Hope traffic is 184% of normal; it rises when ships reroute, so it is shown for context and not scored. Sources: UN Global Platform; IMF PortWatch.
chokepoints.calculation: Per corridor, ratio = 7-day mean daily transits / mean for the same month in 2022-01 to 2023-10. Score = 100 - 300 x sum(tonnage weight x (1 - min(ratio / 0.90, 1))), clipped to 0-100.

geopolitical.description: The Geopolitical Risk index counts newspaper coverage of geopolitical tensions, both threats and acts, across major newspapers each day. Its 30-day average was 176, against a normal level set at the pre-2020 median.
geopolitical.calculation: The 30-day mean of the daily index is mapped on a log scale through its anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 history = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, the record monthly GPR, October 2001 = 0).

energy.source: Brent (DCOILBRENTEU, BZ=F: live, scaled from the 2026-10-20 print); ULSD (DDFUELNYH, HO=F: live, scaled from the 2026-10-20 print); TTF (TTF=F x EURUSD=X: live, converted to $/MMBtu; PNGASEUUSDM monthly average is the fallback)
energy.description: Cost pressure on supply chains from Brent crude, New York Harbor ultra-low-sulfur diesel and European natural gas (TTF), each as a price adjusted for inflation. It measures energy cost pressure, not demand-side health, and a fast run-up in any price costs extra points. Spike penalty this cycle: 3.0 pts. WTI crude is $107.89/bbl (2026-10-20, not scored). Brent minus WTI is $7.33/bbl. The ULSD crack spread (ULSD x 42 minus Brent) is $96.85/bbl.
energy.calculation: Per leg: price x CPI ratio (to 2025-12-01 dollars), log, then mapped through anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, worst monthly average = 0). Weights Brent 35%, ULSD 40%, TTF 25%, renormalized over available legs. Minus the weighted spike penalty: 0 up to a 20% real rise over 91 days, 15 points at 82% or more. Clipped to 0-100.

inputs.name: brent
inputs.source: Brent (DCOILBRENTEU, BZ=F: live, scaled from the 2026-10-20 print)
inputs.raw_value: $118.23/bbl; real price +17% in 3 months, spike penalty 0.0 pts

inputs.name: ulsd
inputs.source: ULSD (DDFUELNYH, HO=F: live, scaled from the 2026-10-20 print)
inputs.raw_value: $5.12/gal; real price +20% in 3 months, spike penalty 0.0 pts

inputs.name: ttf
inputs.source: TTF (TTF=F x EURUSD=X: live, converted to $/MMBtu; PNGASEUUSDM monthly average is the fallback)
inputs.raw_value: $30.61/MMBtu; real price +69% in 3 months, spike penalty 11.8 pts

chip_fab_util.description: Advanced nodes (≤7nm) = 69% of wafer revenue. Supply-constrained.

chip_memory_prices.description: HBM pricing at $16/GB in 2026 (≈+20% renewals). Healthy moderate pricing.
chip_memory_prices.calculation: Bell-curve score centered at $15/GB, extremes penalized

chip_lead_times.raw_label: Avg Lead Time: CoWoS-L, CoWoS-S, CoWoS-S, CoWoS-L, CoWoS-L, CoWoS-S, TSMC N3, TSMC N3, TSMC N3
chip_lead_times.description: Average lead time of 38 weeks for key components (CoWoS-L, CoWoS-S, CoWoS-S, CoWoS-L, CoWoS-L, CoWoS-S, TSMC N3, TSMC N3, TSMC N3) in Q2 2024, Jun 2024, Q4 2024, Q4 2024, Q1 2026, Q1 2026, Q2 2024, Q4 2024, Q1 2026

chip_wafer_prices.description: TSMC TSMC pricing at $16,500 per wafer in 5nm (2020).
chip_wafer_prices.calculation: Bell-curve score — extreme prices in either direction are penalized

aero_metals.description: IMF global aluminum is $3,283/metric ton and nickel is $16,324/mt. Aerospace airframes and superalloys are aluminum- and nickel-intensive; this is a cost-pressure gauge, not a demand gauge. Blended with COMEX aluminum futures (ALI=F $3136) at 30% weight so this category moves between monthly IMF prints.
aero_metals.calculation: Score = average of two inverse percentiles (aluminum, nickel) within the trailing 730-day window, blended 30% with COMEX aluminum futures scored against their own 2-year range. Cheaper than most of the window = high score.

aero_orders.description: Census manufacturers' new orders for nondefense aircraft and parts are $18,825 million this month ($18,686M as a 3-month average). Higher order books read healthier. The average exists because a single widebody order can dominate one monthly print.
aero_orders.calculation: Score = direct percentile of the 3-month average of ANAPNO within the trailing 730-day window. Higher orders = higher score.

aero_production.description: Federal Reserve industrial production for aerospace product and parts (NAICS 3364) is 99.3 (index 2017=100). This measures real output at US aerospace plants, not orders or prices. Higher production reads healthier.
aero_production.calculation: Score = direct percentile of IPG3364S within the trailing 730-day window. Higher output = higher score.

aero_ppi.description: Aircraft manufacturing PPI (PCU336411336411) is 304.7, +2.7% year-over-year. This is a cost-pressure gauge of inflation, not the index level: a high but slowing PPI is less stressful than accelerating producer prices. Faster PPI growth squeezes airframe and engine supply chains.
aero_ppi.calculation: Score = inverse percentile of the year-over-year change in PCU336411336411 within the trailing 730-day window. Slower PPI inflation = higher score. The index level is not ranked — a steadily rising PPI would otherwise pin at 0.

inputs.source: Fed prices paid (FRED: Philadelphia PPCDFSA066MSFRBPHI, Empire State PPCDISA066MSFRBNY); Copper (PCOPPUSDM, HG=F: live, scaled from the Sep 2026 average); Aluminum (PALUMUSDM, ALI=F: live, scaled from the Sep 2026 average)
inputs.raw_value: composite z +1.26 in Oct 2026: Philadelphia 43.2, Empire State 59.5 / $14,335/mt / $3,134/mt
inputs.description: Cost pressure on manufacturers' inputs, not a demand gauge: lower prices read as healthier whatever their cause. The Philadelphia and Empire State Fed manufacturing surveys report the share of firms paying higher prices; each is compared with its own 2004-2019 range and the results are averaged (composite z +1.26 in Oct 2026). Copper is $14,335 per metric tonne (live quote). Aluminum is $3,134 per metric tonne (live quote). Supplier delivery times, context only and not scored (above 0 means slower deliveries): Philadelphia 8.5 (Oct 2026), Empire State 19.8 (Oct 2026).
inputs.calculation: Prices paid: each survey's value minus its 2004-2019 mean, over its sd, averaged over the surveys reporting that month, then mapped through anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 history = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, worst monthly average on record = 0). Copper and aluminum: price x CPI ratio (to 2025-12-01 dollars), log, same anchors. Weights prices paid 50%, copper 25%, aluminum 25%, renormalized over available inputs.

inputs.name: prices_paid
inputs.source: Fed prices paid (FRED: Philadelphia PPCDFSA066MSFRBPHI, Empire State PPCDISA066MSFRBNY)
inputs.raw_value: composite z +1.26 in Oct 2026: Philadelphia 43.2, Empire State 59.5

inputs.name: copper
inputs.source: Copper (PCOPPUSDM, HG=F: live, scaled from the Sep 2026 average)

inputs.name: aluminum
inputs.source: Aluminum (PALUMUSDM, ALI=F: live, scaled from the Sep 2026 average)

tariffs.source: Treasury Daily Treasury Statement customs deposits / goods imports (FRED BOPGIMP); Trade Policy Uncertainty index (Caldara et al.), 30-day mean
tariffs.raw_value: 7.96% of goods imports (3 months to Aug 2026) / 230.0 (30-day mean of the daily index)
tariffs.raw_label: Customs duties as % of goods imports; Trade Policy Uncertainty (30-day mean)
tariffs.description: Customs duties deposited to the US Treasury, paid mostly the month after goods are imported, were 7.96% of goods imports over the three months to August 2026. Deposits are gross of IEEPA refunds, so the burden can overstate what importers end up paying. Trade Policy Uncertainty, a daily index built from newspaper coverage, averaged 230.0 over the last 30 days. For context, the newspaper-based trade policy uncertainty index on FRED (EPUTRADE) was 1212.9 in Aug 2026; it is not scored.
tariffs.calculation: Each input is mapped through its anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 history = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, worst on record = 0): the burden as customs deposits over goods imports, 3-month sums with deposits shifted back one month (month m+1 deposits against month m imports), and the TPU 30-day mean on a log scale. Weights tariff burden 60%, trade policy uncertainty 40%, renormalized over the inputs available.

inputs.name: tariff_burden
inputs.source: Treasury Daily Treasury Statement customs deposits / goods imports (FRED BOPGIMP)
inputs.raw_value: 7.96% of goods imports (3 months to Aug 2026)

inputs.name: tpu
inputs.source: Trade Policy Uncertainty index (Caldara et al.), 30-day mean

freight.source: BTS Freight Transportation Services Index (FRED TSIFRGHT); STB weekly rail carloads plus intermodal units (USDA AgTransport)
freight.raw_value: -2.0% YoY (Jul 2026) / +5.8% YoY (4 weeks to Oct 17; 586,240 carloads and intermodal units that week)
freight.raw_label: Freight volume growth, year over year: BTS Freight TSI; rail carloads plus intermodal units (4-week mean)
freight.description: This category measures goods moving, the demand side of freight: a contraction in volume is bad. It is not a congestion or cost gauge. The BTS Freight Transportation Services Index, the volume of for-hire freight moved by trucks, rail, barges, pipelines and air, was down 2.0% in July 2026 from a year earlier. US railroads originated 5.8% more carloads and intermodal units over the four weeks to October 17 than in the same four weeks a year earlier.
freight.calculation: Each year-over-year growth rate is mapped through its anchors (healthiest 5% of pre-2020 history = 100, pre-2020 median = 80, worst on record = 0). TSIFRGHT is compared with the same month a year earlier; rail is the 4-week mean of originated carloads plus intermodal units against the same mean 52 weeks earlier. Weights BTS Freight TSI 50%, rail volume 50%, renormalized over the inputs available. TSIFRGHT is published about 80 days after its month ends, rail about 5 days after its week ends.

inputs.name: tsifrght
inputs.source: BTS Freight Transportation Services Index (FRED TSIFRGHT)

inputs.name: rail_volume
inputs.source: STB weekly rail carloads plus intermodal units (USDA AgTransport)
inputs.raw_value: +5.8% YoY (4 weeks to Oct 17; 586,240 carloads and intermodal units that week)

physical.source: GDACS Orange and Red alerts near ports; USGS 07010000 Mississippi River at St. Louis
physical.raw_value: 1 active Orange or Red alert / 8.54 ft
physical.raw_label: Active hazard alerts; St. Louis stage (ft)
physical.description: 1 Orange or Red natural-hazard alert is active worldwide today; 1 is close enough to affect a major port (cyclones within 450 km, floods 100 km, earthquakes 150 km, volcanoes 50 km), weighted by the port's share of world port calls. The Mississippi at St. Louis reads 8.54 ft; low stages cut barge drafts and tow sizes.
physical.calculation: Hazards: 100 minus 5000 x the sum, over affected ports, of port-call share x level points (Orange 0.5, Red 1.0), clipped to 0-100. Mississippi: 100 at or above the low-water stage (the gauge's 10th-percentile stage), 0 at its record low, linear between. Weights hazards 67%, Mississippi 33%, renormalized over available inputs.

inputs.name: hazards
inputs.source: GDACS Orange and Red alerts near ports

inputs.name: mississippi
inputs.source: USGS 07010000 Mississippi River at St. Louis
